''For a summary of all translated versions of The Wheel of Time see [[The Wheel of Time translations]].''

The Wheel of Time translates as ''Sagan om Drakens återkomst'' in Swedish. This literally means "The Saga of the Return of the Dragon". Each of the first eleven original books was translated and published in two volumes by the publisher Natur & Kultur in the years indicated in parentheses. 

The two volumes that make up The Eye of the World were translated by Ylva Spångberg. The remaining translations were done by Jan Risheden. 

In 2009, the publisher made a statement that they would not be producing translations of the remaining books, ostensibly because the novels would not be completed by the original author, it would be split into three parts and the end of the story would not be deliverable until 2015.<ref>[http://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagan_om_Drakens_%C3%85terkomst Swedish Wiki Sagan om Drakens återkomst]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141023235358/http://www.catahya.net/nyhet.asp?id=3130 Cataya.net, 24 Oct 2009]</ref>

===Audiobooks===
The translated versions above were also made available as audiobooks and published by StorySide. The Eye of the World through to The Fires of Heaven (Vol. 1-10 in Swedish) were narrated by Viktor Åkerblom and Lord of Chaos through to Knife of Dreams (Vol. 11-22) were narrated by Niklas Engdahl. As they use the same translations, there are also no audiobooks beyond Knife of Dreams. Additionally, there is no audiobook edition of New Spring.
